thread:
alex: Heads up — canary deploy of gpu-workloads in eu-west failed during post-start. Pods crash with config errors, looks like SECRET_* vars got different values after helm render :rotating_light:
jamie: Can you paste the pod logs / pipeline step? /cc @tara @ryan
alex: pipeline log snippet:
```
2026-03-18T10:12:03Z helm template --values values-canary.yaml .
... rendered secret: sops: ENC[AES256_GCM,data:...,iv:...]
kubectl apply -f manifests/canary
Error: container entrypoint failed: missing env: SECRET_MODEL_ENDPOINT
``` 
tara: That points to our values layering — we recently added an env injection in the gitops overlay that mirrors a Vault key. If SOPS overlay and the helm overlay both set the same key, last-applied wins.
ryan: Did Terraform change anything in the k8s secret provider or the vault role? Or was this purely a gitops helm values change?
alex: No TF change in the last deploy window. The only PR merged was in infra-apps/gitops: https://git.example.com/infra-apps/helm-charts/-/merge_requests/842
sophie: We merged a small change to the vault-agent injector last week (to add a new mount path). It should be backward-compatible but could have reordered mounts. I'll check the agent logs on the node.
deploy-bot: AUTO-ROLLBACK: Canary deployment #gpu-canary failed health checks, triggering rollback to rev 12. (reason: env validation error)
jamie: Quick mitigation options: 1) revert the helm values PR, 2) re-encrypt SOPS secret with correct key, or 3) temporarily disable vault-injector for the canary namespace.
alex: Option 3 seems fastest to restore capacity, but we should avoid manual disables if we can. GPUs are idling in CrashLoopBackOff and cost is spiking because autoscaler is replacing nodes :money_with_wings:
ryan: For longer term: add a CI gate to detect duplicate keys between sealed/sops secrets and chart values. We can run a simple diff in the chart-render pipeline.
tara: Example check I can add in the gitops pipeline:
```
helm template --values values.yaml . > rendered.yaml
sops -d secret.enc.yaml > secret.dec.yaml
python scripts/check_key_conflicts.py rendered.yaml secret.dec.yaml
```
sophie: I'll own adding a small linter in the vault-agent repo to log when injected keys collide with existing env values. Also will audit the injector mount ordering change.
alex: Action items: 
- sophie: check vault-agent logs + revert patch if needed (ETA 1h)
- tara: add key-conflict check to gitops CI and open MR (ETA 4h)
- jamie: run quick rollback/disable in canary and verify health (doing now)
- ryan: prepare a small postmortem template capturing cost impact (ETA EOD)

jamie: Ran `kubectl rollout undo deployment/gpu-worker -n canary` and then:
```
kubectl rollout status deployment/gpu-worker -n canary --watch
kubectl get pods -n canary -o wide | grep gpu
```
pods are coming back up, health probe 200 on /internal/ready
alex: Nice. Keep me posted. Once stable let's promote the fix to prod canary policy with the CI check in place.
sophie: Found in agent logs: vault-agent mounted `/etc/vault` then `secret-overrides` later, which overwrote the chart values for SECRET_MODEL_ENDPOINT. Reverting mount order in next patch. Opening MR now and tagging @alex @tara.
tara: I'll also add a test that renders both sources and fails the pipeline if they conflict. That should prevent this overlap going forward.
alex: Thanks everyone — big win getting GPUs back without manual redeploy across clusters. Follow-up: include a small note in the deployment runbook about secret layering and who owns overrides.
ryan: Adding cost impact numbers to the PM doc, will estimate node churn and preemptible reschedules.
jamie: closing the canary incident for now, will re-open if anything flips. :white_check_mark:
sophie: MR: https://git.example.com/vault-agent/-/merge_requests/56
alex: 👍
